answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by weighting reputation by age, not just volume. A new identity starts with almost no voting or earning power, and its weight grows only through months of honest work. Trust is like pigment settling into cloth: a quick dye fades, but color built up layer by layer stays. A harbor does not give a newcomer the berth of a captain who has docked safely for years, and a meadow is not judged by one season. An attacker spawning a thousand fresh identities gains a thousand near-zero weights; each must be tended for months, making the attack slow and expensive.
